decisions.reason: The scenario review says the scenario names the pallet width, height, and depth in metres, and that width and height written as the factory face estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 already matches, params.pallet_width_m and params.pallet_height_m, place that face on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices, beside the admission split this capture already publishes. It says the scenario states no rule that the far side of the mask returns inside that face, chained from the nearest return by steps of one face height, is the pallet depth. sample_face_points keeps the depth returns inside the eroded detection bbox, so a point whose plane projection falls inside the factory rectangle can be the pallet body, a load, the floor, or another object. A load or another surface within one face height of the previous return stays in the window, and that farthest contribution is what the handling process would take as the pallet depth. A gap larger than the face height stops the window at the nearer cluster, including a window that never leaves the face plane. When no return falls inside the rectangle, the proposal names no depth and writes no flag, so a success can reach the handling process with the factory face and no body length. The rejected pocket_opening_depth set has_body_depth false when the openings showed no body. This proposal writes no flag. The feasibility review says a tie for closest to zero has no rule, an empty kept set has no seed while outcome.ok is already true, and a float64 on that message defaults to 0. A face-only cluster leaves depth_m on the order of the 0.005 inlier slab. A foot inside a pocket hole still lies inside the outer rectangle. The recorder stores no width, height, or depth. The restatement review says the proposal does not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms. It is not already kept or rejected. The depth it would publish is a quantity the scenario does not name, and a missing body is an undefined length on a success.

The scenario review says width and height as the factory face sit on the pose result with the admission split. It says depth is the mean optical z of the two fork-opening centres, and that on a frontal face those centres share the range already stored as pose.position.z. On a tilted face the two optical depths differ, and their mean is still the range of two points on the face. The scenario lists depth with width and height and lists the pose on its own. It states no rule that the optical depth of those two centres is the pallet depth, and no rule that those two centres are a result the handling process reads. The handling process would size the approach from a camera range of the openings, including a capture whose depth returns never measured a body behind the face. The rejected pocket_opening_depth read the far-side returns through the openings and could withhold that length. This proposal lifts the prototype hole centres onto the plane and does not read those returns. The feasibility review says the midpoint of the two pocket centres is the prototype origin, the three maps are affine, and the mean of the two RGB centres' z is pose.tz for every theta and every plane tilt. depth_m defined as that mean republishes the face-centre optical range publish_pose already writes. The restatement review says the proposal does not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms. It is not already kept or rejected. The depth it would publish is the pose range, and the two centres are a result the scenario does not name.

The scenario review says width and height as the prototype face, params.pallet_width_m and params.pallet_height_m, place that face on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices. Depth is the face-centre range this call already stores as pose.tz, and publish_pose already copies that scalar into pose.position.z. The same scalar is depth_m. The scenario lists depth with width and height and lists the pose on its own, so copying the face-centre range into depth_m gives the handling process that range a second time under the size listed beside width and height. It states no rule that the optical-frame z of the face centre is the pallet depth, and no rule that a flag true on every published pose marks the three sizes. has_dimensions is true on every success that publishes PalletPoseStamped, and a failed estimate publishes no PalletPoseStamped, so the handling process never reads the flag as a missing body. The rejected inlier_face_extents took depth as the mean z of the plane inliers, which is that face range. This proposal publishes the single face-centre z. The feasibility review says the pass does not read a length along the normal, the false has_dimensions value is never on the published message, and every success publishes the same width and height because the node never changes params_. The recorder already stores pred_tz from pose.position.z. The restatement review says the proposal does not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms. It is not already kept or rejected. The depth it would publish is the pose range this capture already carries.
